The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, anchor, cell and on all six dispositions (kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
The group check's description says the group is active but its query tests only that the name occurs once; activeness is tested by a separate requirement.
The case's hr_service, opened_for and approver are not tested: the request says only 'a US employee', the seed has several US-national profiles (40, 50 and 80 in organisation 1 among them), and hr_profile holds nationality but no work country. ACC-74-33 is also the account number of seed case 34, opened for profile 74 (nationality DE), so it does not identify the employee. 'US' is left out of the description terms because a case-insensitive match on 'us' hits ordinary words.
The request forbids reconfiguring topics, COEs and roles; no available tool writes those tables, so no requirement tests them. Existing payroll rules (4 for GB, 8 for BR) and existing high-priority payroll cases are background the request says to ignore, and no available tool can change them.
The request asks for exactly two criteria whose names begin with the group name; each is tested by its full name, and no count of the prefix is tested.
The negative check holds on the seed by design, since the approval criterion does not exist yet; it guards against misrouting and earns nothing on its own. Like the benchmark's join, it does not count a matching case with no assignment group; the case requirement requires group 19 on the one case created.
The acting user is an admin, whom the policy allows to configure groups, criteria and assignment rules; section 2 of the policy says administrators must not perform routine HR case work, but the validation case serves the configuration the request asks for, so it stands.
